spec: PL-97 WP E2, part a (plan §3.4 E2 and the binding amendments §8.2; the E2 text in §3.4 was rewritten at ed0aaaa0 to be fail-closed). E1a/E1b are landed (BwrapTrampoline backend, select_backend, two-stage trampoline, PathMap, plan_landlock_mapped, merge_reports; read their code and commit messages first). Deliver the runtime contract that E2b and PR #153 build on: (1) an optional, VERSIONED per-job write scope on JobSpec (e.g. `write_scope: Option<JobWriteScope>` with `version: u32` and a list of absolute paths; serde default None for old records); unknown versions are refused at admission/start with a typed error, never ignored. (2) the Linux coordinator maps a present write scope into FilesystemPolicy.read_write (replacing, not widening, the profile's workspace read-write grant: the workspace becomes read-only except the listed paths) before plan_landlock_mapped; paths must be absolute, normalised, inside the job's workspace, and a path that does not exist must be covered by an explicit parent-directory entry (document that the Landlock planner skips non-existent paths); a scope path outside the workspace is refused. (3) fail closed: any job with a write scope, or with SandboxRequirement::Required, is refused BEFORE any process starts when the selected backend cannot enforce the filesystem dimension (backend None or Bwrap without Landlock, or a Landlock ABI that cannot express the rules); only legacy unscoped BestEffort jobs may run on a weaker backend, logged once. Scoped jobs always carry SandboxRequirement::Required. (4) fix `job_resources` in coordinator/linux.rs so every JobSpec resource maps: memory_max, memory_high, cpu_max, cpu_weight, pids_max, io (whatever JobResources/cgroup.rs support) plus rlimits into the trampoline plan; unsupported dimensions are reported, not silently dropped. (5) config `[sandbox] execution = "chain" | "legacy"` (default chain; profile scope; an untrusted project layer cannot set it; add it to the FIELD_TABLE, merge rule, exhaustive test and docs/design/config-structure.md). It is only parsed and exposed here; E2b consumes it. (6) the security-review requirement for E1: the job must never get Landlock write access to the attempt directory destination (`/run/harw-job/attempt`); verify E1b honours this and add a test asserting the mapped policy never contains it as read-write. Tests: write scope round-trip + old record without the field; unknown version refused; out-of-workspace path refused; mapped policy = workspace ro + listed rw; scoped job with backend None refused with no process started (use the coordinator's existing fake/test hooks); BestEffort unscoped job still runs on None; job_resources maps all fields; config scope rows.

spec: PL-97 WP E2, part b (plan §3.4 E2, amendments §8.2). Builds on E2a (versioned JobSpec write scope, fail-closed refusal, full job_resources mapping, `[sandbox] execution`). Today shell.exec (harw-tool-shell/src/exec.rs ~725-834) pre-builds `prlimit … -- bwrap …` and submits it as CommandSandbox::Host; job.start goes the same way through ShellJobLauncher (harw-tool-job/src/launcher.rs, delegating to ShellToolProvider::prepare_background_launch); child agents (job_child_backend.rs) run as plain host processes via JobManager::start_piped with executed_on_host: true. Deliver, when `[sandbox] execution = "chain"` (default): (1) shell.exec and job.start submit a JobSpec with program /bin/sh -c <cmd> (exactly today's shell semantics), cwd = workspace, a SandboxPolicy derived from the tool's SandboxSpec (workspace rw/ro, NetworkMode, cargo/tmux modules via the SandboxProfile modules and HostPathBinding -- extend BwrapExecutor::plan / plan_with_trampoline to accept those so nothing shell.exec can do today is lost), a ResourceRequest from ShellLimits (2 GiB memory, cpu 60 s, fsize 256 MiB, nofile 256, nproc 4096, tmpfs 256 MiB), timeout -> deadline, stdio piped; keep today's output caps, truncation, cancel and exit-code semantics exactly. (2) child agents: JobChildBackend submits with SandboxProfileName::WorkspaceBuild (or the role's profile when one exists) and executed_on_host = false; the child's job record then carries a cgroup path (C4a JobStatus::cgroup_path). The host-permit path (run_host_command / `!` host mode) stays the only CommandSandbox::Host submission. (3) `execution = "legacy"` keeps today's code path byte-for-byte. (4) fail closed per §8.2: an unscoped legacy-style call may fall back to the weaker backend with one logged warning per session (`runs without cgroup/landlock`), but any call that carries a write scope or Required is refused with a clear tool error and no process. (5) Do not invent new approval paths; existing approvals for shell.exec/job.start stay exactly as they are. Tests: a recording fake port receives exactly one JobSpec per shell.exec/job.start call with the expected policy, resources and deadline; output/timeout/truncation parity against the existing spawn_and_collect fixtures; legacy mode uses the old path; a child agent submission is not executed_on_host and requests WorkspaceBuild; scoped call with no enforcing backend returns an error and starts nothing.

spec: PL-97 WP E3 (plan §3.4 E3, amendments §8.2 E1 install lists and E3 user unit) plus the E1b release follow-ups. Deliver: (1) `harw_job_runtime::host::resolve_delegated_root(config, env) -> RootResolution { root: Option<PathBuf>, source: Config|Env|OwnCgroupDelegated|None, hint }` with order `[jobs] cgroup_root` (new key, profile scope, trusted layers only; an untrusted project layer cannot set it) -> HARW_CGROUP_ROOT env (keep HARW_VERIFY_CGROUP_ROOT working as a deprecated alias for the verify runner) -> the process's own cgroup if HostReport says cgroup_v2_delegated -> None with the hint to start harw under `systemd-run --user --scope -p Delegate=yes …` or enable the service units; the root must be an absolute path under the cgroup2 mount, else refused with a typed error. (2) JobCommandPort::host / install_host_default (harw-command/src/global.rs, called from harw-runtime/src/job_wiring.rs and harw-cli/src/chat.rs) pass the resolved root into LinuxExecutorOptions.cgroup_root; None keeps today's no-cgroup behaviour with one logged hint. (3) systemd: harw-control.service gets Delegate=yes (and DelegateSubgroup=harw.slice only if the repo's systemd baseline is >= 254 -- check docs/setup; otherwise document the systemd-run route); the rendered harw-serve user unit (harw-install/src/service_systemd.rs) gets Delegate=yes and passes the cgroup root (env or config); update harw-install parity fixtures. (4) `harw dod config suggest` prints, for the resolved root R, the DoD profile stanza (scope = "cgroups", cgroup_paths = ["<R absolute>"], include_descendants = true, sensors = ["exec","tcp-connect"]) and the matching harw `[dod] allowed_cgroup_prefixes = ["<R>"]`; `--drop-in` prints a sentinel unit drop-in with `--cgroup-root <R>`; `harw dod doctor` warns when the active DoD profile does not cover R or when allowed_cgroup_prefixes is not within R. Canonical prefix form: absolute path under the cgroup2 mount, with a documented converter to the Warden's relative CgroupId; DodSection::validate rejects the relative form. Wiring prefixes into the Warden's ProofPolicy stays out of scope (PL-96 W01) -- say so in docs/setup/dod.md. (5) Release/install lists ship harw-job-exec next to harw: Makefile RELEASE_PACKAGES, scripts/package-release.sh, scripts/install.sh --binary, .github/workflows/release.yml; `harw doctor` (harw-install/src/doctor.rs) reports a missing harw-job-exec. Starting services stays an explicit operator action (make service); nothing new starts at install. Tests: resolver order with fake env/config/host report; non-absolute or outside-mount root refused; suggest output golden (both forms); doctor warnings; parity fixtures; doctor reports missing trampoline.
